paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Integrity starts at home. David sings about the LORD's loving devotion and justice (Psalm 101:1), and then he says, "I will walk in my house with integrity of heart" (Psalm 101:2). Anybody can look good at the city gates. David starts where nobody is clapping.

Notice that David's promises are about what he lets near him. He will set "no worthless thing before my eyes" (Psalm 101:3). He turns away from a perverse heart, from slander, from pride and from deceit (Psalm 101:4-7). I think that means integrity is less about one big moment and more about a hundred small choices about what gets a seat at your table. And I'll be honest, a lot of us let in things we'd never invite on purpose.

But David isn't only closing doors. His eyes favor "the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me" (Psalm 101:6). And he doesn't wait for someday. He says, "Every morning" (Psalm 101:8). So ask yourself, baker: what's one thing in your home or heart that needs showing out, and who is one faithful person you can make room for? Start this morning, because integrity is a daily habit, and you can start again tomorrow.
